evidence: Entry 0x4080e4 decrypts strings using 0x407080. The helper seeds the Delphi PRNG, obtains high32((state*0x08088405+1)*255) per byte and XORs the buffer.

0x40759c enumerates drives; 0x4074b4 recursively walks files; 0x4071d0 selects EXEs, checks MZ, transforms the displaced prefix and replaces it with its own viral body before appending the saved prefix at EOF. File attributes are cleared for access and restored.

0x4079a0 copies the viral body into the Windows directory as svchost.com, decodes exefile\shell\open\command, opens HKCR and writes a default command consisting of the installed path plus the original target and argument placeholders. This is EXE-launch persistence, not a login Run key.

0x407678 reconstructs the host from the EOF prefix and intervening host body, decrypting the first 1000 saved bytes with a seed at prefix offset 1234. The output is opened through ShellExecuteA with the platform verb open.

Recovered host SHA256 253ae12bfc92844114dc8965a7bf9452ca7271c7e6b91828630f3e84aa56399b has an intact Intel Corporation signature and identifies Intel Common User Interface/IGFXCUISERVICE.EXE, version 6.15.101.5522.

No bytes establish the many unrelated malware families in the collector-assigned basename. Distribution context is unknown; unauthorized executable infection and handler hijacking independently establish the verdict.

evidence: SHA256 is identical to testdata/triage/ime-pe-arcade-20261025/pixel-loader.cs. The artifact is one internal class with a private, uninvoked Load method; it supplies neither image bytes nor a payload or entry point.

The method reads the first row of caller-provided pixels, shifts in each blue-channel low bit, writes each group of eight bits into a MemoryStream, saves ToArray() to the supplied path, and starts that path. The low eight bits of the accumulator supply each output byte.

The behavior is a risky concealed-byte loader demonstration, not concrete theft, spying, destruction, backdoor operation or deception. Unknown caller/image deployment context prevents attributing an attack; the comment alone does not determine the verdict.
The shared matcher binds only the save/start path and uses proximity for pixel reads and low-bit arithmetic. It does not prove pixel-to-output flow or an attacker-controlled stage.

evidence: Forager retrieved pkg:golang/github.com/microsoft/pxt@v3.5.8+incompatible from proxy.golang.org and verified h1:0QqFjuUblgErEZ9Xynl/F5LbKOa5rQihhCF8HYwwqDk= against sum.golang.org. Recovered ZIP SHA256 ac5c65856a637ec5b5d7c954215d36f1e25cd7a14c03b066a92c8ae48c6b813e exactly equals the supplied archive.

package.json build/test/start hooks invoke Jake. Jake invokes local TypeScript/Mocha/Karma build and test commands; it assembles the PXT CLI, compiler, simulator and web editor. There is no concealed install hook.

CLI initGlobals/initCommands registers explicit commands. Login stores and retrieves only pxt/<target> Keytar credentials. CI release paths use operator-provided npm/GitHub/Crowdin tokens for publishing; the temporary .netrc addition supports git upload and is restored afterward.

external/tdast.js is the bundled TouchDevelop runtime/AST converter. testConverterAsync loads it for td2ts conversion. Its eval sites activate supplied compiled TouchDevelop scripts or worker precompiled code; setup initializes APIs and the lexer. This behavior fits the documented compiler/runtime role. Embedded Base64 image data and tutorial source are assets, not independently established concealed execution.

The two ML probability-1.0 members are ordinary UWP package.appxmanifest files. They declare MakeCode/localhost StartPages, documented content access and Internet/removable-storage/serial/HID/Bluetooth capabilities for programming boards. Manifest declarations are not executed attacks.

Fetched GitHub behaviors and react-core asset SHA256s match independent forager downloads. These are normal rspack/webpack browser UI bundles, not archive modifications. Isolated scans before and after have H0/S0 and identical traits.

limits: New persistence and decoy composites correlate evidence within a file; they do not resolve registry handles or shell-open argument provenance. Descriptions retain that limitation.
The reassembly matcher covers the reviewed Delphi register/stream idiom, not all possible infector implementations.
The encoded association matcher covers the documented length-seeded LCG representation; arbitrary keys and algorithms are not claimed.
The large TouchDevelop file exceeds the source-flow byte budget, so manual eval/caller tracing and exact upstream provenance support its review.
